tldr: In the two-cell, three-treatment affine Bernoulli benchmark, the exact critical adoption frontier is proved for the selected policy's population mean-squared conditional outcome gaps. For \(n\tau_n\to\kappa^2\), maximal causal welfare regret converges to \(r(\kappa)=\{1-\mathcal A(\kappa^2/(2\sigma^2))\}/10\). A normalized shrinking-prior posterior proof gives a nonasymptotic lower bound against every original-record Borel Markov rule; an explicit total rule is exactly globally \(0.05\)-honest at every sample size and attains the critical limit. The scalar switches, adoption-support necessity, joint continuity, and sharp joint scalar stability orders are proved. Matching original-record stability follows above the posterior and calibration errors, with sufficient condition \(n^{-7/32}=o(\epsilon_n)\); finer scales retain a proved computable bracket. The benchmark motivates prospective group-blind entrepreneurship-program planning and is distinct from the published classes of Kock--Preinerstorfer and Bian et al.
